newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bundestag relaunches tax reforms.
newsitem.headline: German Bundestag relaunches tax reforms.

text.p: Germany's Bundestag lower house of parliament voted on Tuesday to relaunch government tax reforms which had been blocked by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) in parliament's conflict-resolution process.

After an ill-tempered debate, deputies from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition voted to overturn a decision by the SPD-controlled parliamentary mediation committee to reject its plan for sweeping cuts in income and corporate taxes.
The Bundestag also voted with an overwhelming majority in support of a cross-party compromise struck in the mediation committee to abolish a capital trading tax on companies.
But the coalition majority combined to vote down an SPD initiative calling for a cut in occupational insurance charges intended to boost job creation.

The Bundestag was recalled from its summer recess to vote on Finance Minister Theo Waigel's 30 billion mark package of income tax cuts, which had been blocked by the SPD first in the Bundesrat upper house and then in the mediation committee.

Waigel said he would invoke a second round of parliamentary mediation but opposition parties said they would not accept his reforms and called instead for Kohl to call early general elections to clear Germany's tax deadlock.
